use_hint: Fix the sentence · Enter = check · Enter = next
note: B2 grammar unit, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane, replacing the empty stub. 35 items, inside the 24-40 band. C57: card 1 recaps Second and Third conditional, the two units this one crosses. The teaching point is the TIME MISMATCH, so the unit is built as two named shapes with their own blocks — past cause -> present result (15) and present cause -> past result (14) — rather than one undifferentiated bank. Both halves are drilled: block 1 gaps the result auxiliary on eleven items and the if-half `had` on four, so the student cannot pass by always typing the same word. D1 is respected deliberately: every item carries its OWN explanation naming its own words and why the time is where it is. The live b2_third_conditional pastes one string across dozens of items and is on the repair queue for exactly that; this unit does not clone the fault. Distractors stay on the axis (B6) and the unit's own error — would have where would belongs, and vice versa — is on the board (B4). A5: `were` and `was` both accepted throughout the second-conditional half; A8 contractions accepted in every `accepts` list. Use is error-correction (E7), each prompt carrying one real error (E2): the would-have/would swap, `had took`, and `would` inside the if-clause, which is the commonest Czech-learner error in conditionals. KEY WORD TRANSFORMATION: this unit is on the KWT-native table in codex/FCE-EXERCISES.md, but KWT needs a js/ branch that is interactive/James-only under P-engine, so the Use stage here is ordinary error-correction and the KWT question is logged in DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Mixed conditionals
points: One half is in the **past**, the other half is in the **present**.
Fact: I didn't study medicine, so I am not a doctor.
Unreal: If I **had studied** medicine, I **would be** a doctor now.
The two halves do not have to sit in the same time.

rows: I didn't study medicine. I am not a doctor.
If I **had studied** medicine, I **would be** a doctor now.
I am not organised. I missed the flight.
If I **were** more organised, I would not **have missed** the flight.
She didn't take the job. She lives here.
If she **had taken** that job, she **would live** in Berlin today.

cards.title: You already know
cards.title_cz: Už znáš — druhý a třetí kondicionál
points: **Second conditional** keeps both halves in the present or future.
**Third conditional** keeps both halves in the closed past.
A mixed conditional takes one half from **each**.

cards.title: Past cause, present result
points: The **if** half is the closed past: **had** + past participle.
The result half is **now**: **would** + verb — never *would have*.

rows: we **would be** at home by now.
If he **had gone** to bed earlier,

cards.title: Present cause, past result
points: The **if** half is a standing fact about now: **were**, **had**, or past simple.
The result half is one finished event: **would have** + past participle.
*were* and *was* are both heard in this half.

rows: I would not **have missed** the flight.
we would **have visited** you last week.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: *Would* never appears in the **if** half — in any conditional.

rows: ~~…I would have been a doctor now~~
